title: CI/CD Is Dead, Agents Need Continuous Compute and Computers — Hugo Santos and Madison Faulkner
talk_summary: A VC and an infra CEO argue that agent-scale code generation breaks PR-based CI/CD because human-latency assumptions (warm caches, one diff at a time, serialized merges) no longer hold. They propose moving validation into the agent's inner loop, replacing human PR review with specialized reviewer agents, and adding a serialized pre-merge queue that reconciles many parallel branches before a human approves intent-vs-result rather than code.

takeaways.technique: Validation inside the agent loop, not after the PR
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent harness checks out a known commit, builds and tests the change itself each iteration, and only then reports back, so CI is no longer a separate phase after handoff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it goes and uses the assets that exist in the repository to actually validate that the change is correct. So, it builds it. It has tested.

takeaways.technique: Specialized reviewer agents feeding the inner loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one human/one generic review, multiple narrow agents (security-focused, API-conformance) give feedback directly into the coding harness's loop, which incorporates it before merge.

takeaways.technique: Serialized pre-merge queue with semantic grouping
takeaways.what_they_do: Completed changes go to a pre-merge queue that reconciles parallel branches touching the same code to guarantee serializability, then groups multiple agent changes semantically for one human approval of intent-vs-result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need a process that reconciles them so that you can have serializ- serializability

takeaways.technique: Stateful, warm environments instead of cold starts
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue the inner loop must run in stateful environments with retained memory/state, because restarting from scratch every iteration adds latency; agents should work incrementally like engineers on workstations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're starting things from scratch all the time, you're just going to delay things even further. So, the statefulness of it is really important

takeaways.technique: Codified intent/spec as the unit of work
takeaways.what_they_do: Work starts from a written intent/plan (ticket or Slack) that the harness loops against, and the harness re-adapts the plan when world signals change (plan changed, someone else merged).
takeaways.evidence_quote: We start with intent and plan. This is what we want to achieve and we codify it. That's the spec.

takeaways.what_they_do: Even in the fast loop they keep compliance invariants: agents must start from a well-known commit and cannot introduce unvetted code, enforced every iteration rather than once at CI.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you still want to have guarantees that you're starting from a well-known uh checkout
